name: United Kingdom
travelAdvice: Type G sockets are standard. Check every device label for 230 V support before connecting it.

name: United States
travelAdvice: Types A and B are standard. Devices from 220–240 V regions must explicitly support 120 V.

name: Canada
travelAdvice: Types A and B are standard. Confirm that imported appliances support a 120 V, 60 Hz supply.

name: Australia
powerNote: The nominal supply is 230 V, although 240 V may still appear in labels and older references.
travelAdvice: Type I sockets are standard. Check the input range on devices brought from lower-voltage countries.

name: New Zealand
travelAdvice: Type I sockets are standard. Verify voltage support as well as plug fit before using a device.

name: Japan
powerNote: Eastern Japan generally uses 50 Hz and western Japan generally uses 60 Hz.
travelAdvice: Most sockets accept Type A, while grounded Type B availability varies. Check devices for 100 V support.

name: China
powerNote: This record covers mainland China; Hong Kong and Macau use different socket systems.
travelAdvice: Types A and I are commonly listed for mainland China. Do not assume a plug fitting means the voltage is safe.

name: India
travelAdvice: Types D and M are used, with Type M associated with higher-current appliances. Use a suitable grounded adapter.

name: Thailand
travelAdvice: Several socket types are in use, including Thailand's Type O. Carry an adapter matched to your accommodation.

name: Singapore
travelAdvice: Type G sockets are standard. Check device voltage labels before use, especially for high-powered appliances.

name: France
travelAdvice: Types C and E are used. Grounded devices need an adapter that correctly connects the Type E earth contact.

name: Germany
travelAdvice: Types C and F are used. Grounded appliances require a compatible grounded connection, not only a two-pin fit.

name: Spain
travelAdvice: Types C and F are used. Check voltage compatibility before connecting devices from 100–120 V countries.

name: Italy
travelAdvice: Types C, F, and L are used. Socket availability varies, so a versatile grounded adapter is useful.

name: Brazil
powerNote: The local supply may be 127 V or 220 V and can vary by location. Confirm it at the property before use.
travelAdvice: Type N is the national standard and Type C is also used. Always confirm the local voltage and device label.

name: United Arab Emirates
travelAdvice: Type G sockets are standard. Devices from 100–120 V regions need an input rating that includes 230 V.

name: South Africa
powerNote: Type N is being adopted alongside the established Type M system; socket availability can vary.
travelAdvice: Types C, M, and N may be encountered. Confirm the available socket and use a properly rated grounded adapter.
